extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent attorneys, patent classifiers, applicants preparing classification information
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for classifying patent documents in Cooperative Patent Classification subclass G16H (healthcare informatics): scope, specific group scopes (10/00–80/00), and exclusion/assignment rules distinguishing G16H from medical classes such as A61 and A61B. Useful for deciding whether ICT-related medical inventions belong in G16H or in medical/device classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subclass scope: healthcare informatics (G16H)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subclass covers cross-sectional aspects of computer, information or communication science with medical or healthcare science, where the focus is clearly placed on digital computing or data processing systems or methods, which are specially adapted for medical or healthcare science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this subclass when the essential technical features focus on digital computing or data processing systems or methods specially adapted for handling or processing medical or healthcare data. (Notes omitted in header may contain further clarifications.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions — medical methods/equipment and diagnostic signal processing
rubrics_metrics.description: This subclass does not cover: a. medical equipment, medical methods, methods of diagnosis, methods of treatment or therapy, clinical care or surgical procedures per se, which are covered by the relevant subclasses of A61; b. signal processing or signal transmission associated to diagnostic measurements, e.g. signal waveform analysis, which are covered by group A61B 5/00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subject matter is essentially a medical device, clinical method, surgical procedure, or purely signal processing associated with diagnostic measurements, classification should be directed to the appropriate A61 (or A61B) groups rather than G16H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification rule — essential technical features must focus on digital computing/data processing
rubrics_metrics.description: To classify a technical subject in this subclass it is required that the essential technical features of the subject focus onto digital computing or data processing systems or methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the invention's essential technical features — if the digital computing/data processing aspects are central (not incidental), G16H is appropriate. Mere incidental use of computing is not sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification tie-breaker — focus on medical science or patient interaction → A61
rubrics_metrics.description: If the technical subject focuses onto aspects of medical science, e.g. physiological signals or medical conditions, or if the subject involves a significant interaction with the patient, e.g. details of a diagnostic measurement, then classification shall be directed to the appropriate subclasses of class A61.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the invention's primary contribution is in medical/physiological aspects or patient-facing measurements/processes, prefer A61 even if ICT is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not-key-element rule — mere presence of a computer or flowchart insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere presence of "a computer" or "a flowchart" in relation to medical devices or procedures is not a key element for classifying in this subclass. In this case classification shall rather be directed to the appropriate subclasses covering those medical devices or procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not classify into G16H solely because a computer/flowchart is mentioned; determine whether the ICT adaptation itself is the essential inventive feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-limiting references warning
rubrics_metrics.description: In this subclass non-limiting references (in the sense of paragraph 39 of the Guide to the IPC) may still be displayed in the scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that cross-references shown in the scheme may be non-limiting; use the textual notes and rules to decide proper placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group 10/00 scope — ICT for handling or processing patient-related medical/healthcare data
rubrics_metrics.description: 10/00 — ICT specially adapted for the handling or processing of patient-related medical or healthcare data (for medical reports G16H 15/00; for therapies or health-improving plans G16H 20/00; for the handling or processing of medical images G16H 30/00).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes electronic clinical trials or questionnaires; data related to laboratory analysis (e.g. patient specimen analysis); patient-specific data such as electronic patient records; storage on portable record carriers (smartcards, RFID tags, CD). Subgroups (10/20, 10/40, 10/60, 10/65) cover specific subtopics listed in the scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group 20/00 scope — ICT for therapies or health-improving plans
rubrics_metrics.description: 20/00 — ICT specially adapted for therapies or health-improving plans, e.g. for handling prescriptions, for steering therapy or for monitoring patient compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers systems relating to drugs or medications (ensuring correct administration, delivered from dispensers or via infusion/injection), relating to physical therapies or activities (physiotherapy, acupressure, exercising), mechanical/radiation/invasive therapies (surgery, laser therapy, dialysis, acupuncture), nutrition control (diets), mental therapies (psychological therapy, autogenous training), and alternative medicines (homeopathy, oriental medicines). Refer to subgroup codes (20/10, 20/13, 20/17, 20/30, 20/40, 20/60, 20/70, 20/90) for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group 30/00 scope — ICT for handling or processing medical images
rubrics_metrics.description: 30/00 — ICT specially adapted for the handling or processing of medical images (computed tomography A61B 6/03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes systems for handling medical images (DICOM, HL7, PACS) and for processing/editing medical images. Use 30/20, 30/40 etc. for specific image-handling or processing functions; note cross-reference to A61B 6/03 for CT-related matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group 15/00 scope — ICT specially adapted for medical reports
rubrics_metrics.description: 15/00 — ICT specially adapted for medical reports, e.g. generation or transmission thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this group for systems focused on creating or transmitting medical reports; see 15/00 group entries for detailed subtopics relevant to report generation/transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group 40/00 scope — ICT for management/administration and operation of medical equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: 40/00 — ICT specially adapted for the management or administration of healthcare resources or facilities; ICT specially adapted for the management or operation of medical equipment or devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes management/administration of healthcare resources/facilities (managing hospital staff, surgery rooms), management of medical equipment/devices (scheduling maintenance/upgrades), and operation of medical equipment/devices. Use subgroup codes (40/20, 40/40, 40/60, 40/63, 40/67) to distinguish local vs remote operation and specific management functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group 40 note — operation must include data transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: This group covers ICT specially adapted for the operation of medical equipment or devices, or of their interfaces, i.e. aspects of the operation where the focus is on the processing of medical or healthcare data which results in contextual, content-related or structural transformation of said data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not classify in 40/00 if the operation of equipment/interfaces occurs without contextual/content/structural transformation of medical data — such cases are covered by the relevant groups of class A61.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group 50/00 scope — ICT for diagnosis, simulation, data mining, epidemics
rubrics_metrics.description: 50/00 — ICT specially adapted for medical diagnosis, medical simulation or medical data mining; ICT specially adapted for detecting, monitoring or modelling epidemics or pandemics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes computer-aided diagnosis (medical expert systems), calculating health indices and individual health risk assessment, simulation or modelling of medical disorders, mining of medical data (analysing previous patient cases), and detecting/monitoring/modelling epidemics or pandemics (e.g. flu). Use subgroup codes (50/20, 50/30, 50/50, 50/70, 50/80) for specific activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group 70/00 scope — ICT for handling or processing medical references
rubrics_metrics.description: 70/00 — ICT specially adapted for the handling or processing of medical references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers references relating to practices or guidelines, to drugs (side effects or intended usage), and to pathologies. Use subgroup codes (70/20, 70/40, 70/60) to identify the specific type of reference material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group 80/00 scope — ICT for facilitating communication between practitioners/patients
rubrics_metrics.description: 80/00 — ICT specially adapted for facilitating communication between medical practitioners or patients, e.g. for collaborative diagnosis, therapy or health monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify systems that enable collaborative workflows, telemedicine-style communication, coordinated diagnosis/therapy, or patient-practitioner communication under this group.
